title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Took a Call From Donald Trump in the Middle of an All-Hands
gist: Trump personally called Jensen Huang mid-all-hands to congratulate him on Nvidia's blowout Q2 (revenue $96B, up 106% YoY), underscoring the White House's direct, high-touch relationship with Nvidia just as the company launched a political PAC and reportedly moved to acquire Hugging Face for over $13B amid unresolved US-China chip export tensions.

insights.claim: President Trump personally called Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's mobile phone in the middle of a company all-hands meeting, loud enough for staff to hear Trump's voice through Huang's onstage microphone, according to three witnesses.
insights.speaker: Lauren Goode
insights.so_what: A sitting president interrupting a corporate all-hands to speak directly with a CEO signals an unusually direct, personal political relationship for a company central to AI infrastructure and export-control policy.
insights.quote: President Donald Trump interrupted Nvidia's all-hands staff meeting on Thursday morning when he called CEO Jensen Huang midway through, three sources who witnessed the interaction tell WIRED.

insights.claim: Trump publicly congratulated Huang on social media the same day for Nvidia's 'incredible' quarterly sales and its rosy financial forecast for the following year.
insights.speaker: Lauren Goode
insights.so_what: Public presidential praise for a specific company's earnings is a notable signal of political alignment that investors may read as reducing near-term regulatory/export risk for Nvidia.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'In a post on social media later that day'

insights.claim: Huang regularly travels to Washington to lobby government officials on behalf of Nvidia's interests in chip sales and AI infrastructure buildout, and has previously held closed-door meetings with Trump.
insights.speaker: Lauren Goode
insights.so_what: Establishes an ongoing, institutionalized lobbying channel between Nvidia and the administration, relevant context for handicapping future chip-export and AI-regulation decisions.
insights.quote: Huang regularly jet-sets to Washington to lobby government officials on behalf of his company's interests—selling chips and building AI infrastructure—and has been in closed-door meetings with Trump before.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'Huang regularly jet-sets to Washington'

insights.claim: Nvidia and the Trump administration have not always agreed on how to regulate open AI models and sales of advanced chips to China, even as the two sides maintain close contact.
insights.speaker: Lauren Goode
insights.so_what: Flags China chip-export policy as an ongoing point of friction rather than a settled matter, meaning Nvidia's China-exposed chip revenue remains subject to policy swings despite the close personal relationship.
insights.quote: Nvidia and the Trump administration haven't always agreed on how to regulate open AI models and sales of advanced chips to China.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'Huang regularly jet-sets to Washington'

insights.claim: Nvidia reported second-quarter revenue of $96 billion, up 106 percent year-over-year, disclosed the day before Trump's call to Huang.
insights.speaker: Lauren Goode
insights.so_what: A concrete, current revenue figure and growth rate for Nvidia directly relevant to valuing the company and gauging AI infrastructure spending momentum.
insights.quote: On Wednesday, Nvidia had reported second-quarter revenue of $96 billion, up 106 percent from the same period last year.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'In a post on social media later that day'

insights.claim: On the same day as Trump's call, Nvidia announced a new employee-funded political action committee that will donate to federal candidates as AI policy debate intensifies.
insights.speaker: Lauren Goode
insights.so_what: Nvidia is formally scaling up its political spending apparatus, indicating the company expects AI and chip-export policy to remain a high-stakes, contested issue requiring sustained lobbying investment.
insights.quote: Earlier on Thursday, the chip giant announced a new employee-funded political action committee, through which it plans to donate to federal candidates as debate around AI policy grows.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning 'But the president's direct call'

insights.claim: The Information reported that Nvidia agreed to acquire the open-source AI platform company Hugging Face, which provides widely used AI data sets, models, and development tools to software engineers.
insights.speaker: Lauren Goode
insights.so_what: A Hugging Face acquisition would give Nvidia direct control over a key open-source AI distribution layer that much of the developer ecosystem depends on, extending its moat beyond hardware into software/model distribution.

insights.claim: Business Insider reports the Nvidia-Hugging Face deal could be valued at more than $13 billion, and would almost certainly require merger approval from US antitrust regulators.
insights.speaker: Lauren Goode
insights.so_what: A deal of this size triggers antitrust review, so regulatory posture toward Nvidia -- which the Trump call and PAC news suggest is currently favorable -- becomes directly relevant to deal-completion risk and timeline.
insights.quote: An acquisition could be valued at more than $13 billion, Business Insider reports, which would almost certainly require merger approval from US antitrust regulators.
